name: Hemolytic Anemia Due to an Erythrocyte Nucleotide Metabolism Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Hemolytic Anemia Due to Erythrocyte Nucleotide Metabolism Disorder

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficient erythrocyte nucleotide metabolism enzyme activity
Clinical and laboratory evidence of chronic hemolytic anemia (elevated reticulocytes, low hemoglobin, increased LDH)
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding erythrocyte nucleotide metabolism enzymes
Exclusion of other common causes of hemolytic anemia such as autoimmune hemolysis or membrane defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of enzyme deficiency and clinical hemolytic anemia with genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of biochemical, clinical, and genetic data.

laboratory: Reduced activity of erythrocyte nucleotide metabolism enzymes (e.g., adenylate kinase, nucleotidase)
Elevated serum indirect bilirubin and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)
Elevated erythrocyte nucleotide degradation products in blood or urine
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding erythrocyte nucleotide metabolism enzymes (e.g., AK1 gene mutations)
other: Exclusion of autoimmune hemolytic anemia by negative direct antiglobulin test (Coombs test)

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of spherocytes on peripheral blood smear

redFlags: Severe anemia with rapid hemoglobin drop
Signs of acute hemolytic crisis (e.g., dark urine, jaundice)
Unexplained splenomegaly in a child with anemia
